title: Everyday Digital Skills: Your Phone, Your Money, Your Business
summary: Practical skills for life and work, learned on your own phone at your own pace: make your phone faster and cheaper to use, send and receive money without being scammed, sell on WhatsApp and Google Maps, and keep your accounts safe. For traders, artisans, parents and anyone learning for themselves. No experience needed.
outcomes: Set up a phone so it is locked, up to date, has space and uses less data
Send money by app, USSD or POS and check the receiver before paying
Recognise common payment scams and know what to do in the first minutes after one
Set up WhatsApp Business with a catalogue and automatic messages
Take clear product photos with any phone and get a business found on Google Maps
Write a clear, professional email and protect accounts with strong passwords and two-step verification
prerequisites: A smartphone (Android or iPhone) you can practise on. Reading at a basic level. Everything else is explained step by step.

lessons.title: Check: your phone
lessons.intro: Five quick questions. You can try again as many times as you like.

questions.prompt: What is the safest way to lock your phone screen?
options: A pattern drawn on the screen
A PIN of at least 6 digits, or a fingerprint with a PIN behind it
No lock, so you can open it quickly
questions.explanation: A longer PIN is hard to guess; patterns can often be read from finger smudges.

questions.prompt: Why should you install phone and app updates?
options: They fix security holes criminals use
They are needed only for new phones
questions.explanation: Updates close weaknesses that criminals know about.

questions.prompt: Which uses NO data from your bundle?
options: Downloading a video on trusted Wi-Fi
Sending WhatsApp videos on mobile data
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi does not use your mobile data bundle.

questions.prompt: Where should you NOT open your bank app?
options: At home on your own Wi-Fi
On an open Wi-Fi network with no password that you do not trust
On your office Wi-Fi that your company manages
questions.explanation: Untrusted open Wi-Fi can be watched by others; use your mobile data for banking.

questions.prompt: Your phone is nearly full and slow. What helps first?
options: Deleting unused apps and large WhatsApp videos after backing up what you need
questions.explanation: Freeing space makes the phone faster and lets it save new photos and messages.

lessons.title: Scams and how to stop them
Lab: spot the scam message
lessons.intro: Look at each message and decide whether it is safe or a scam. Look closely at the sender, the link and what it asks you to do.

questions.prompt: Before you press send on a transfer, what must you check?
options: The receiver's name shown by the bank, the amount and the bank
Nothing: transfers can always be reversed
questions.explanation: The name shown by your bank confirms you are paying the right account.

questions.prompt: A customer shows you a screenshot of a transfer and wants to leave with the goods. What do you do?
options: Check your own bank app or official bank alert for the money first
Ask them to send the screenshot again
questions.explanation: Screenshots and SMS alerts are easy to fake. Only money you see in your own account is real.

questions.prompt: Someone calls 'from your bank' and asks for the code you just received by SMS. What should you do?
options: Hang up and call the bank on the number on your card or official website
Ask them to call back later and then give it
questions.explanation: Banks never ask for your OTP, PIN or password. Call them yourself on the official number.

questions.prompt: A stranger says they sent money to you 'by mistake' and asks you to send it back to another account. What is safest?
options: Check your own balance and, if money really arrived, ask your bank to reverse it
Give them your BVN so they can check
questions.explanation: This is a common trick. Let your bank handle real mistaken payments.

questions.prompt: Money has left your account that you did not send. What do you do FIRST?
options: Wait a few days to see if it comes back
Post about it on social media
Call your bank's fraud line at once to block the account and trace the transfer
questions.explanation: Minutes matter: the bank can sometimes stop or trace the money if you call immediately.

questions.prompt: Which offer is almost certainly a scam?
options: A shop's posted price for rice
An 'investment' that doubles your money in two weeks
Your bank's app asking you to log in after an update you installed from the app store
questions.explanation: Promises of fast, guaranteed profit are a classic sign of a scam.

lessons.title: Good product photos with your phone
Check: selling online
lessons.intro: Five questions about selling with your phone.

questions.prompt: What is a greeting message in WhatsApp Business?
options: A message sent automatically to new customers
questions.explanation: It welcomes new customers and tells them how to order, even when you are busy.

questions.prompt: Which makes the best product photo?
options: Daylight from a window, plain background, clean lens
A photo copied from another seller's page
A dark room with the brightness turned up afterwards
questions.explanation: Good natural light and a plain background make products clear. Copying photos is dishonest.

questions.prompt: How can customers see the size of a product in a photo?
options: Show it in a hand, being worn, or next to a common object
questions.explanation: Something familiar next to the product shows its real size.

questions.prompt: Someone calls offering to 'verify' your Google Business Profile for a fee. What do you do?
options: Ignore it: Google does not charge to list a business
questions.explanation: Listing on Google Business Profile is free; these calls are scams.

questions.prompt: A customer leaves a bad review. What is the best response?
options: Reply politely and offer to put it right
Pay for fake good reviews to hide it
questions.explanation: A calm, helpful reply shows future customers you care. Fake reviews are dishonest and can get you removed.

lessons.title: Final check
lessons.intro: Eight questions from the whole course. Pass this, with the other checks, to finish the course.

questions.prompt: Which is the strongest password?
options: my goat eats mango every friday
questions.explanation: Long passphrases are easy to remember and very hard to guess.

questions.prompt: Why use a different password for each important account?
options: If one website is hacked, your other accounts stay safe
questions.explanation: Reused passwords let criminals open every account with one stolen password.

questions.prompt: What does two-step verification do?
options: Asks for a second thing, like a code, so a stolen password is not enough
Shares your account with a friend
questions.explanation: A criminal who has your password still cannot get in without the second step.

questions.prompt: Which email subject is best for a job application?
questions.explanation: A clear subject tells the reader exactly what the email is about.

questions.prompt: How should you send a CV by email?
options: As a photo of the screen
As a PDF with a clear name such as Your-Name-CV.pdf
questions.explanation: PDFs look the same on every device, and a clear name helps the reader.

questions.prompt: A job advert asks you to pay for a 'processing form' before the interview. This is…
options: A warning sign: real employers do not charge you to get a job
A sign of a high salary
questions.explanation: Paying to get a job is a common scam.

questions.prompt: A code arrives by SMS that you did not ask for. What should you do?
options: Share it with whoever calls about it
Do not share it; someone may be trying to get into your account
Reply to the SMS with your PIN
questions.explanation: Unexpected codes often mean someone is trying your password. Never share them.

questions.prompt: Which saves the most data on WhatsApp?
options: Auto-downloading all videos on mobile data
Setting media to download only on Wi-Fi
questions.explanation: Videos are large; downloading them only on Wi-Fi saves your bundle.
